newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel to pay France, UK 25 pct of profit.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel to pay France, UK 25 pct of profit.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc said on Tuesday that it would pay around 25 percent of net profit after 2052 to the British and French governments in exchange for an extension to its licence.
Eurotunnel executive chairman Patrick Ponsolle said in a statement, "the participation of the governments in the company's profits after 2052 should be around 25 percent of the profits after tax.
"I am very happy for our shareholders for the declaration by the French and British governments concerning Eurotunnel's concession," he said.
An extension to the licence to at least 99 years would allow shareholders "to expect a satisfactory return on their initial investment," he added.
The efforts to increase rail traffic through the Tunnel should not affect the rail revenue forecasts contained in the restructuring prospectus, he said.
The company aimed to conclude a final agreement on these issues before a planned capital increase and the issue of free share warrants for the current shareholders, he said. pnt
The French finance ministry earlier said the French and British governments were ready to extend Eurotunnel's licence to at least 99 years, citing certain conditions.
Those conditions included the governments getting a share of Eurotunnel's profits after 2052 when the extension would kick in and an increase in rail freight traffic.
Shareholders and creditor banks must also approve the plan to restructure Eurotunnel's 70 billion francs of bank debt. Shareholders vote on the plan on July 10.

The current licence runs for 65 years. Eurotunnel needed to get the extension to win shareholders' backing for the debt deal, which involves a dilution of the equity capital down to 54.5 percent through a share rights issue.
Eurotunnel has said it would issue one free warrant for every eight shares, exercisable to 2003, if the licence were extended.
